mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the destination state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. If the destination state is not a party to the Apostille Convention, have the certificate notarized by a New Zealand Notary Public and then submit it to the destination state's embassy or consulate in New Zealand for consular legalization. These two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention members: issue an Apostille from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. For non-members: notarize the certificate before a New Zealand Notary Public, then legalize by the consular post of the destination state in New Zealand. Choose only one path, never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of NZ_LTD (to be executed by the first directors upon incorporation and notarized)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize director signatures before a New Zealand Notary Public. Then, if the destination country is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille from MFAT. If the destination country is not a member, apply for consular legalization at its embassy or consulate in New Zealand. The apostille and consular legalization procedures are mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: NZ_LTD (registered constitution lodged with the New Zealand Companies Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A notarized copy of the registered Constitution must be certified by a New Zealand Notary Public. Thereafter, for destinations that are Apostille Convention members attach an Apostille issued by MFAT; for destinations that are not Apostille members, undertake consular legalization through the destination state's diplomatic mission in New Zealand. Do not combine both processes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed New Zealand registered bank maintaining the company's corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank officer's signature and capacity must be notarized by a New Zealand Notary Public. For Apostille member states, complete the process with an MFAT Apostille; for non-member states, complete the process with consular legalization at the destination state's consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are separate, parallel channels and must not be performed sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Subject to New Zealand's Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and the United Nations Security Council sanctions regimes, every proposed director, shareholder, beneficial owner, and authorized signatory must be screened before incorporation against consolidated lists published by the New Zealand Police FIU, the U.S. Department of the Treasury OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, and the United Kingdom's financial sanctions list if applicable. Positive PEP matches require enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and independent verification of source of funds and source of wealth. Screening shall be repeated at commencement of business and at least annually thereafter; results must be documented and retained for five years under the AML/CFT Act 2009.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office — Company Name Search and Reservation portal (online via Business.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin alphabet characters (A-Z) and Arabic numerals; Māori words are permitted, and any non-Latin script name must be transliterated into Latin script as it will appear on the Companies Register. The name must be capable of being read and spoken in English, must not be identical or almost identical to an existing registered or reserved name, must not include restricted words without prior statutory body approval, and must end with "Limited" or an approved suffix such as "Ltd" or "Tapui (Limited)" for a limited liability company. The four-tier naming convention comprises (1) prohibited-word screening, (2) distinctiveness and non-identicalness testing, (3) offensiveness and misleading-content prohibition, and (4) special endorsement requirements for regulated tokens.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives written reasons citing the Companies Act 1993 s 22(4). An administrative review may be requested by writing to the Reviewer, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE), within 20 working days of the rejection notice, attaching the original confirmation, a statutory declaration, and evidence of legitimate commercial use or consents from affected parties. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, a further appeal may be made to the High Court of New Zealand under section 22A(4) of the Companies Act 1993. For restricted-token refusals, the applicant must first obtain ministerial or agency approval (for example from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand) and resubmit. The rejected name is not reserved during the appeal unless an interim reservation extension is expressly granted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not absolutely prohibited under the Companies Act 1993 for the registered office, but it is rejected by Inland Revenue and the principal New Zealand banks for this ISIC 3240 manufacturing activity. For GST registration, corporate bank account opening, and commercial substance verification, IRD and banks demand a physical New Zealand operating address demonstrating local floorspace, die-casting or warehousing capability, and a named person on site during business hours. A virtual office may be acceptable only as a supplementary communications address; relying on it as the sole registered or tax address will trigger enhanced due diligence, likely account refusal, and higher audit scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) correct physical street address, not a PO Box, on register, tax and bank records; (2) lease or ownership evidence in the company's name; (3) business identification at the premises; (4) tangible manufacturing assets such as zinc alloy die-casting moulds, tampo printing equipment, or scale-model inventory; and (5) a responsible person available during working hours. Quantified risk: unannounced inspections by the Registrar of Companies and Inland Revenue occur in approximately 2–3% of compliant low-risk manufacturing companies, but where a virtual office is detected the probability rises to 12–15% with consequential penalties, GST de-registration, and potential deregistration under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (N.Z.), ss. 12, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 22, 44, 84, 87, 122, 128, 131, 140, 153, 189 and Schedule 1; Companies (Name Reservation) Regulations 1994; Financial Reporting Act 2013; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Form NZCN1), and Declaration of Director and Shareholder Consent Forms (NZCN2)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or blocked escrow account requirement under the Companies Act 1993. The subscribers may set the issued share capital freely; the minimum capital is discretionary and fully determined by the allotment resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS IN WRITING OF THE FIRST BOARD MEETING OF [●] LIMITED (COMPANY REGISTRATION NUMBER [●]) BY THE SUBSCRIBED DIRECTOR(S) PURSUANT TO SECTION 189 OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993. 1. RESOLVED that the constitution be adopted as the supreme contract under section 122 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. RESOLVED that notice of registered office be filed with the Registrar. 3. Any two signatories to act jointly for amounts exceeding NZ$[●], or other authorizations per board rules. All of the foregoing resolutions were passed unanimously and shall be effective as from the date of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name reservation and preparatory governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (online Register), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search of the Companies Register to determine whether the proposed name 'NZ NZ LTD' is identical, similar, or prohibited under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. File a company name reservation and obtain a reservation number valid for 20 working days. Simultaneously draft a bespoke constitution or elect the default constitution in Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993; prepare and execute consents to act as directors and shareholder declarations. For any foreign signatory, provide notarized evidence of identity and a certified English translation if the source document is not in English; however, notarization is not mandatory for straightforward New Zealand registration.
required_dossiers: Draft constitution or default Schedule 1 constitution
Consent to act as director form (Form NZCN2 or registered agent form)
Certified copy of passport for foreign director/shareholder
Proof of physical street address for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, within five working days file a new name reservation with alternative permitted names or request a direction from the Registrar; if constitution is queried, amend to align with the Companies Act 1993 mandatory provisions and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory filing of incorporation application and certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the formal application for registration of a company, Form NZCN1, through the New Zealand Companies Office online portal, attaching the reserved name, constitution, director consent forms, and the registered office address (a physical street address). Verify that at least one director is a resident of New Zealand or Australia and that the primary administrative office is in New Zealand. Sign the form by authorized subscribers and pay the required filing fee by credit card or POLi. Upon validation, the Registrar of Companies registers the company and issues the certificate of incorporation, which is conclusive evidence of existence under section 18 of the Act. Foreign documents must be accompanied by notarized endorsed translation if not in English.
required_dossiers: Form NZCN1 Application for Registration of a Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, the Registrar will issue a defect notice; within 10 working days submit corrected forms and explanations. If registration is refused, apply for review by the High Court of New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue tax registration and ACC levy
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (myIR portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the certificate of incorporation, apply to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number, GST registration (if gross income over NZD 60,000 per annum or voluntarily), and employer registration for PAYE/ACC. Provide the certificate of incorporation, constitution, and director particulars. The application is made using the myIR portal and is typically completed online. Directors must confirm the company's tax residency and maintain records for income tax returns under the Tax Administration Act 1994. For a company with offshore directors, provide individual tax numbers and notarized copies of identity documents; all correspondence must be in English. Update IRD with any subsequent changes.
required_dossiers: Directors personal tax details and IRD forms (IR596)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD application is delayed or suspended, contact the IRD helpdesk with reference number; provide any missing individual tax information; if a tax number is not allocated within five working days, escalate to IRD complaints and use a tax agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account activation and AML/KYC finalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Bank under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate transaction account with a registered bank or non-bank lender in New Zealand, presenting the certificate of incorporation, the constitution, the engrossed board resolution authorizing account opening, and identity documents for all directors and beneficial owners. Complete the bank's customer due diligence questionnaire under the AML/CFT Act 2009, including source of funds and expected transaction volumes. Determine the mandated signatory structure, for example, any one director or two joint signatories, and execute a bank mandate accordingly. If any document originates outside New Zealand, an apostille and a certified notarized English translation are required. Retain the authorized signatories list and update the bank within ten days of any officer change.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the application, request a written reasons statement, remedy any documentary gaps, or in the alternative open an account with a non-bank lender or different registered bank; if suspicious activity refusal persists, retain a legal opinion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Local territorial authority land-use and building consent for manufacturing facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial Authority (City or District Council) and, if applicable, building consent authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain land-use and building approval from the territorial authority having jurisdiction over the planned manufacturing facility. Submit the floor plans, structural engineers' report for die-casting equipment, geotechnical and seismic assessment, fire safety design, and hazardous substances storage layout. Under the Resource Management Act 1991, apply for a land-use consent if the site is not zoned for heavy manufacturing; if not exempt, the authority may require limited notification or full notification. Building consent under the Building Act 2004 ensures compliance with the Building Code; obtain a code compliance certificate after construction and before commencing operations. All drawings and calculations must be stamped by a chartered professional engineer.
required_dossiers: Structural and seismic loading report for die-cast machines
Fire engineering report and means-of-escape plans
Site zoning certificate / land-use consent application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If consent is refused, request mediation under the Resource Management Act 1991, or appeal to the Environment Court within 15 working days; if building consent is suspended, correct compliance defects and re-inspect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, hazardous substances, and fire safety permits pre-operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Council, Environmental Protection Authority, and Fire and Emergency New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure environmental and emergency operating permits. File a scope-of-works and discharge permit application with the regional council and, if relevant, the Environmental Protection Authority, covering wastewater from zinc casting, cooling water, degreasing chemicals, and tampo printing ink solvents. The EIA will classify the facility under Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act and require a site-specific environmental impact assessment, including potential heavy metal deposition on soil and receptors. Clearance from Fire and Emergency New Zealand must cover the flammable inks and die-casting lubricants under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996. The final authorization certifies the company to operate the die-casting and tampo printing process lawfully.
required_dossiers: Resource consent application forms and site plan
Hazardous substances inventory and safety data sheets
FENZ building fire safety inspection checklist
HSNO location approval or compliance certificate
Trade waste discharge application to local wastewater authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resource consent is not granted, update the management plan with lower discharge loads, install best practicable option technology, submit an amended EIA, and appeal to the Environment Court; for HSNO non-compliance, appoint a compliance certifier and obtain site verification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Territorial Authority (City/District Council) in coordination with the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) and WorkSafe New Zealand
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Resource Consent for Industrial Trade Process (manufacturing and discharge) and Building Code Compliance Certificate for a Die-Casting and Industrial Printing Facility

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of New Zealand acting jointly with the relevant Regional Council responsible for resource consents
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment - Category B: mandatory site-specific EIA for heavy metals, volatile organic compounds (VOC), and hazardous substances, submitted as a regional discharge application or equivalent district plan resource consent
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: zinc <1.0 mg/L, lead <0.5 mg/L, total suspended solids <100 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0; Air emissions: total particulate matter <10 mg/m3, zinc airborne concentration <5 mg/m3, VOCs subject to best practicable option and detected via stationary source sampling; Hazardous waste: disposed via an approved waste-tracking facility under the HSNO Act; spill containment of 110% of largest storage container required

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) Certificate of Fire Safety for industrial occupancy; statutory structural clearance for high-load die-casting machines; WorkSafe New Zealand outdoor and indoor hazardous substance location certificate; regular sweep and inspection under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tāke) of New Zealand; online electronic portal: myIR at ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident company deriving New Zealand-sourced income or undertaking taxable activity in New Zealand must obtain a New Zealand IRD number. For a non-resident company not incorporated in New Zealand, the prescribed application is the Inland Revenue non-resident company registration process, typically via Inland Revenue form IR596 (Non-resident Company IRD Number Application). The application requires certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office address, directors' names and contact details, ultimate beneficial ownership particulars, and, where a fixed place of business exists in New Zealand, details of the New Zealand agent or representative. Applications may be lodged electronically through myIR where the entity can establish an account or by paper submission to Inland Revenue, after which the IRD number is issued and used for income tax, GST, employee withholding, and other tax compliance obligations. For New Zealand-incorporated limited companies, the Companies Office automatically exchanges registration data with Inland Revenue, and the company receives an IRD number as part of incorporation without a separate application unless one is required for special domestic law purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A New Zealand limited company is subject to entity-level taxation at the corporate income tax rate of 28%. The principal statutory pass-through election is the Look-Through Company (LTC) election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, available to a New Zealand resident company with no more than five shareholders, all of whom must be individuals or qualifying trust estates; once elected, the company is treated as fiscally transparent, and profit/loss flows through to shareholders. New Zealand resident companies also operate an imputation credit account system that attaches imputation credits to dividends, but no discretionary check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists; New Zealand's hybrid and branch mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 operate automatically to deny deductions for tax outcomes arising from hybrid financial instruments and hybrid entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; a separate NZD 60,000 threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services supplied to New Zealand resident consumers during any 12-month period. Once the threshold is exceeded, compulsory GST registration is required; voluntary registration may be allowed where the business carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand or supplies remote services to New Zealand residents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, API e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate. GST-registered businesses must file GST returns electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR system on a two-monthly, six-monthly, or, for larger businesses, one-monthly filing basis. Tax invoices must comply with the content requirements of section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including supplier name and GST number, date, supply description, amount, and GST charged. E-invoicing via the PEPPOL network is voluntary in New Zealand and is not a compliance clearance mechanism; the anti-fraud regime in New Zealand relies on GST return matching, invoice documentation audits, and Inland Revenue data analytics rather than electronic invoice authentication.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of goods for export is available under section 11(1)(a) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the goods are supplied by a GST-registered supplier and are exported by the supplier to an overseas destination within 28 days after the time of supply. Services supplied to a non-resident outside New Zealand are zero-rated under section 11A, provided the services are not supplied in connection with New Zealand land or moveable personal property situated in New Zealand, and the supplier holds written records sufficient to establish the recipient's non-resident status. Remote services supplied by a non-resident to a New Zealand GST-registered recipient are zero-rated in B2B transactions where the recipient provides their GST registration number; supplies of remote services to New Zealand resident consumers are subject to GST at 15% and do not qualify for export zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration in the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (CUS export entry message) evidencing physical export of the goods from New Zealand
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing the port or airport of loading in New Zealand and the overseas destination of the goods
Commercial invoice and sales contract evidencing the supply of the zinc alloy die-cast scale model automotive replicas to the overseas buyer
Packing list and proof of export within the 28-day statutory window
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 bank credit confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency proceeds from the overseas buyer for the exported goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export zero-rating cannot be substantiated with the required customs and foreign exchange documentation, Inland Revenue may reassess the supply as taxable at 15% GST, claw back any input tax credits claimed, and impose shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Shortfall penalties range from 20% for failing to take reasonable care or taking an unacceptable tax position, up to 150% for evasion or a dominant purpose of tax evasion. Interest on unpaid tax accrues under the use-of-money interest rules. Additionally, incorrect export declarations may trigger prosecution by the New Zealand Customs Service under the Customs and Excise Act 2018, and the statutory time bar for reassessment is generally four years but is extended indefinitely where tax evasion or fraud is involved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ). The RBNZ is the central bank and prudential regulator of registered banks under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989. It is also co-supervisor for AML/CFT purposes together with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. For foreign exchange, New Zealand operates an open, unregulated market: the RBNZ does not issue exchange-control licences, imposes no surrender obligations, and administers no capital-account approval regime. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible under IMF Article VIII. The only substantive gatekeeper for foreign direct investment is the Overseas Investment Act 2005 (OIA) administered by the Overseas Investment Office (Land Information New Zealand), which applies to sensitive land and significant business assets above statutory thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. There are no exchange-control approvals, no central bank licences for trade remittances, and no restrictions on repatriation of dividends, branch profits, or liquidation proceeds. Practical profit-remittance hurdles are purely fiscal: (i) non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at 15% on fully imputed dividends, generally reduced to 5%–15% under New Zealand's double tax agreements, e.g., the NZ–China DTA provides 5% where the recipient holds at least 10% of the voting power, otherwise 15%; (ii) NRWT of 15% on interest and royalties, subject to treaty relief and the approved issuer levy (2%) alternative on interest; (iii) thin capitalisation limitation on interest deductibility for non-resident-owned groups, with a 60% debt-to-asset safe harbour for income years beginning on or after 1 July 2023; and (iv) the requirement that the New Zealand entity hold sufficient imputation credits for dividends to be described as fully imputed. There is no withholding tax or capital gains tax on the disposal of shares in a New Zealand trading company by a non-resident seller unless the shares are land-rich or the disposal falls within the five-year bright-line/land-related property rules. A company incorporated in New Zealand is tax-resident under section YD 2 of the Income Tax Act 2007 even if managed offshore, which preserves treaty eligibility and demonstrates OECD BEPS substance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. New Zealand repealed all foreign-exchange surrender requirements in the 1980s. An exporter of die-cast scale automotive models is under no statutory obligation to repatriate, convert, or surrender export proceeds within any timeline. The exporter may retain NZD or any foreign currency in a registered-bank foreign-currency account or an offshore account. Compliance obligations are limited to: (i) filing complete export entries through New Zealand Customs Service using the Trade Single Window for each shipment for statistical, tariff, and biosecurity purposes; (ii) applying a GST zero rate to export invoices under section 11(1) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 with evidence of exportation within the statutory timeframe; (iii) disclosing proceeds as revenue in financial statements and income tax returns; and (iv) providing the receiving bank with a lawful purpose description on inbound wires, typically SWIFT purpose code 'TCQ' or 'Trade settlement', for AML/CFT record-keeping under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Transfer pricing rules in Part 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007 require arm's length pricing and currency terms for export sales, and the New Zealand resident company must demonstrate real economic substance for OECD/multinational group credibility.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-Low as a primary treasury rail. New Zealand has no passporting regime for non-resident electronic money institutions: an offshore EMI, such as a UK or EU EMI, cannot hold itself out as a New Zealand registered bank and cannot provide core transactional banking services in New Zealand. The use of offshore fintech platforms such as Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business, and HSBC Global Wallet is legally permissible for ancillary collections, multi-currency wallets, and small-value payables, but viability is qualified: (i) New Zealand registered banks apply cautious de-risking to pay-through arrangements and often require the EMI to maintain its own segregated account with a local registered bank; (ii) PayPal inbound settlement into a New Zealand bank is permitted and common for low-risk e-commerce collectibles, provided PayPal is identified as the originator with a 'Trade' or 'Retail goods' purpose code; (iii) PayPal merchant receipts are treated as ordinary trade revenue but lack the documentary robustness of SWIFT MT103 wires, so monthly reconciliation and invoice traceability are essential for AML/CFT comfort; and (iv) the entity should maintain its primary operating account, borrowing facilities, letter-of-credit lines, and ISDA hedging relationship with a prudentially regulated New Zealand bank. Feasibility rating: auxiliary cross-border rail – Medium; sole treasury solution – Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand AML/CFT law and the RBNZ AML/CFT Code of Practice require registered banks to complete customer due diligence before establishing a business relationship. For a New Zealand private limited company, banks typically require: (i) certified true copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, Constitution, and Companies Office extracts including the register of directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial ownership; (ii) identity verification of each director and substantial shareholder; (iii) a face-to-face or bank-approved video interview with at least one principal director or the entity's nominated AML compliance officer; (iv) proof of physical operating premises such as a warehouse or office lease; and (v) a documented source of funds for the opening deposit and anticipated transaction profile. Non-resident directors may complete verification remotely using a notarised and apostilled passport plus a certification by a New Zealand Justice of the Peace or a registered New Zealand solicitor, but prevailing local practice requires at least one director or authorised officer to attend a branch interview in person or to complete an RBNZ-compliant video KYC session. Remote sign-online account opening packages for non-resident-owned companies are offered by ANZ, BNZ, and Westpac, but the bank reserves the right to demand a physical meeting and will decline the account if there is no verifiable economic nexus to New Zealand, significant goods-trade activity, or credible local supply-chain substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is tax-resident in a FATF high-risk or grey-listed jurisdiction, or the ownership chain above NZ_LTD contains opaque nominee structures, shell companies, or trusts whose beneficiaries are not clearly identified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete, current, and annotated Companies Office disclosure; a signed group structure chart identifying every intermediate entity and natural-person UBO; an extracted UBO register from the New Zealand Companies Register; notarised and apostilled passports and proof of residential address for all natural persons; a solicitor's certificate confirming UBO identification under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; a detailed source-of-wealth statement supported by verifiable independent evidence such as audited financial statements, bank statements, sale and purchase agreements, probate documents, or trust deeds; and a letter from the NZ_LTD directors confirming that all foreign entities maintain valid economic substance in their own jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A large lump-sum capital injection into a newly incorporated or previously dormant shelf company with no trading history, often occurring immediately before the first die-cast container shipment or coinciding with a change in beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A board resolution authorising the capital injection and specifying the exact purpose, such as acquisition of zinc alloy, injection-moulding tools, tampo printing machinery, first inventory purchase orders, and working capital; an executed share subscription agreement or documented shareholder loan agreement with interest and term; a capital call spreadsheet reconciling the injected amount to committed purchase orders; management or provisional accounts showing the funding need; a commercial contract or supplier proforma invoice evidencing the immediate trade application; the prior bank statement trail of the investing shareholder; CRS/FATCA self-certification forms; the New Zealand IRD number and GST registration certificates of NZ_LTD; and a written confirmation that the Overseas Investment Act 2005 thresholds were assessed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicators: over- or under-invoicing of die-cast scale models, declared unit values inconsistent with market benchmarks, unexplained freight routes, mismatched Incoterms, or settlements by unrelated third-party payments for export shipments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete per-shipment trade file containing the commercial invoice, packing list, original bill of lading or airway bill, New Zealand Customs Service export entry, insurance certificate, warehouse receipt, and the signed purchase order; the OEM trademark licence agreement proving legitimate authorisation to produce 1:18 scale replica vehicles (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930); third-party unit-cost benchmark analysis referencing typical ex-works prices for zinc-alloy 1:18 die-cast collectibles; the Incoterms clause expressly matching the payment terms in the commercial contract; and, where a third party pays, the buyer's written payment instruction, the payer's bank confirmation, and an inter-company set-off or novation agreement explaining the commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person (PEP) exposure: a supplier, licensee, buyer, or distributor appearing on any New Zealand, United Nations, EU, UK, or US sanctions list, or a PEP involvement in the target distribution market, which would trigger enhanced due diligence and possible account declination.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated and manual sanctions and PEP screening records for all counterparties; negative-media and open-source verification results; a signed declaration from each counterparty confirming it is not a PEP and is not sanctioned; an export-control classification memo confirming the product is a civilian collectible (non-military) under ISIC 3240/NAICS 339930; a New Zealand legal opinion confirming UN and New Zealand sanctions status; inclusion of sanctions, PEP, and anti-money-laundering warranties and termination clauses in all distribution agreements; and evidence that no restricted jurisdictions are part of the payment chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PayPal inflows labelled 'goods' without a verifiable order trail, repeated refund and chargeback anomalies, fungible cross-border flows, or a rapid growth of PayPal receipts relative to SWIFT trade wires in a low-risk collectibles e-commerce model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform-level reconciliation files linking each PayPal transaction ID to an e-commerce order ID, the buyer's shipping address, carrier tracking number, and delivery confirmation; the PayPal seller verification and merchant agreement; the site's refund and chargeback policy; a preserved chargeback history and the management response timeline; a documented daily liquidity sweep from PayPal to the New Zealand registered bank; a narrative explaining any refund spikes, such as pre-order cancellations or limited-edition allocation changes; and a monthly signed officer certification delivered to the bank relationship manager confirming that PayPal receipts represent genuine arm's length retail sales of collectible automotive models.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital into NZ_LTD must be routed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank positioning) from the investing shareholder's bank to the entity's New Zealand registered account. The wire instruction should carry: (i) SWIFT Category Purpose Code 'CT' (Capital Transfer) or 'TC' (Trade) with free-text description 'Equity subscription / shareholder loan to NZ_LTD – ISIC 3240 die-cast collectibles manufacturing'; (ii) the New York or Sydney correspondent settlement account of the receiving New Zealand bank with the correct BIC for the New Zealand branch; (iii) the beneficiary account in the name of NZ_LTD with the IRD taxpayer number on file; (iv) pre-advice to the relationship manager of the supporting board resolution, share subscription agreement, shareholder loan agreement, and proposed use of funds so the bank can classify the receipt as capital rather than assessable revenue; and (v) a prior assessment under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 where the investor is acquiring 25% or more of a New Zealand business and the 'significant business assets' threshold (NZ$100 million for a non-consortium investor, NZ$200 million for a consortium investor, in each case excluding land) is exceeded. New Zealand imposes no exchange-control reporting on the receiving bank for capital inflows; however, NZ_LTD must record the capital in a dedicated capital escrow category in its books, maintain the Companies Office share register update, comply with thin capitalisation rules on any shareholder debt, and disclose related-party cross-border balances in the annual International Dealings Schedule if the shareholder loan is from a non-resident related party.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier payments covering zinc alloy, moulds, tampo inks, tooling, and sub-assembly services, predominantly to Guangdong and Hong Kong vendors, the primary clearing rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 high-value wire transfers for supplier prepayments and invoice settlement, using purpose code 'TC' and the description 'Trade settlement – raw materials for die-cast scale models'; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit opened as revolving irrevocable documentary credits (MT700) for large, repetitive orders, with negotiation against full set clean-on-board bills of lading, signed commercial invoice, and packing list; (iii) bank trade finance suites such as import lines and shipping guarantees where the New Zealand bank funds the documentary payment and releases the goods in transit; (iv) domestic and regional telegraphic transfers in USD or CNY via the foreign-currency account for smaller vendors; and (v) PayPal for direct-to-consumer sales of 1:18 collector replicas, with USD balances swept daily to the NZD operating account. For European and North American wholesale buyers, inbound settlement should arrive by SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'TCQ' and references to the commercial invoice, the buyer's customs import entry, and the Incoterms; larger buyers may pay by letter of credit or documentary collection in accordance with ICC UCP 600 and ISBP 745. All outbound and inbound trade payments must be supported by the underlying shipment file (invoice, packing list, bill of lading, customs entry) to eliminate trade-based money-laundering red flags and to preserve GST zero-rating evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD-USD FX Forwards executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with the New Zealand registered bank, covering committed export receivables and import payables up to 12–24 months; such forwards are fully permissible without RBNZ approval and may be designated as cash-flow hedges under NZ IFRS 9.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referenced to CNY, TWD, KRW, INR, and other restricted or partially convertible Asian currencies, cash-settled in NZD or USD, used to hedge settlement exposures to Chinese die-casting suppliers, tampo-printing subcontractors, and OEM tooling vendors where onshore deliverability is unavailable.

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) converting a USD-denominated trade facility into NZD floating-rate funding, or swapping NZD import payables into USD payables, with notional principal exchanges matched to the underlying trade cycle; the RBNZ imposes no transaction registration, but the bank will apply ISDA credit support annex margin terms and the instruments must be reflected in the treasury policy and board-approved risk management framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NZ Companies Office Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due within 20 working days after each anniversary of the company's incorporation date; specific date stated in annual return notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 200; continued non-compliance for 6 months may result in removal from the Register and strike-off of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements (if required to be filed under Companies Act 1993 or Financial Reporting Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be delivered to the Registrar within 20 working days of filing the Annual Return for the relevant accounting period; accounting period generally ends on the balance date specified
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under Companies Act 1993, fines up to NZD 10,000 for directors; continued failure may lead to registration of a charge or court enforcement; persistent non-compliance can result in strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: IRS/RBNZ/IRD Annual Confirmation of Registered Office and Agent (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Annual Return; any change of registered office or agent must be notified within 10 working days of change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties for late notice up to NZD 50 per day; non-compliance may be treated as a compliance breach affecting good standing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit required for reporting entities under the Financial Reporting Act 2013: companies with total assets exceeding NZD 3 million, or total revenue exceeding NZD 5 million in each of the two preceding accounting periods; also required for entities that are issuers, large companies, or that meet the 'large' threshold under the Companies Act 1993 (assets > NZD 60m or revenue > NZD 30m)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1 entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) for Tier 2 entities; Simplified Financial Reporting for Small and Medium-sized Entities (SME) under the Financial Reporting Act 2013

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand maintains a public register of significant shareholders (register of ultimate beneficial owners) under the Companies Act and Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) provisions; every company must keep a register of shareholders and notify the Registrar of any change in shareholding or UBO details within 10 working days of the change; annual confirmation is required on the annual return, including a list of all current shareholders, number of shares, and any relevant transfers during the reporting year
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBO Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Typical annual registered agent/office fee range: USD 200-600
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Typical certified audit fee range: USD 3,500-8,000 for a die-cast toy manufacturing company (depending on complexity and revenue)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax incentive (15% of qualifying expenditure), no statutory tax holidays
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory year limit; subject to shareholder continuity requirement of 49%)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically via Inland Revenue's myIR secure online portal (peak eyes on ird.govt.nz)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (income tax return) with three provisional tax instalments during the year; year-end balance date typically 31 March
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July following the tax year end; non-standard balance dates are due the 7th day of the fourth month after the balance date; a registered tax agent may obtain an extension of time to file (generally up to 31 March of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Income – aggregate all gross income from sales, fees, commissions, interest, dividends, rents, royalties, and any other source, including worldwide income for a tax-resident NZ company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NZ-incorporated companies are automatically tax-resident; report worldwide income. Non-resident shareholders are not filers on this form. Only transactions with non-residents must be recorded on arm's length terms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Expenditure – deductible expenses incurred in deriving assessable income, excluding non-deductible items (e.g. capital expenditure, 50% of entertainment expenses not meeting exceptions, taxes of a similar nature to income tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportion expenses strictly on an arm's length basis; charges for head-office services, management fees, or IP royalties must satisfy transfer pricing documentation thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net Profit or Net Loss – Taxable profit (or loss) before deduction of prior-year losses and before allocating tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a net loss is declared, the loss carryforward claim is contingent on the 49% shareholder continuity test; disclose changes in shareholding during the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation Credits and Tax Credits – dividends received (with imputation credits), RWT on interest, and any other refundable credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) deducted at source from NZ-sourced dividends, interest, or royalties must be reconciled here if the company is the recipient; reverse hierarchy rules apply for interest paid to non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income – net profit (Box 3) less carried-forward losses after applying continuity requirements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special non-resident provision; the company is assessable on worldwide income, and any treaty protection only applies at the shareholder/residency level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income Tax Payable – calculated at 28% of taxable income, reduced by provisional tax paid and attached credits, resulting in terminal tax due or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Terminal tax is due by 7 April if the return is filed by 7 July and terminal tax is below NZ$2,500; for larger terminal tax, instalment dates under the provisional tax rules apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: NZ$50 per month or part month, capped at NZ$250 for most returns (companies may face NZ$250 per month for large taxpayers, capped at NZ$1,250). Late payment penalty: 1% of the unpaid tax at the due date plus 1% per month thereafter. Use-of-money interest (UOMI) also applies at the prescribed underpayment rate until payment is made.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (statutory rate; may be reduced under an applicable double tax agreement).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must provide the NZ payer with a valid Certificate of Residence (IR13) issued by the foreign tax authority before payment. The payer then applies the DTA rate at source. If full NRWT (30%) has been withheld, the recipient must file a New Zealand non-resident income tax refund claim with Inland Revenue within the statutory four-year time bar, supplying the certificate and treaty position analysis. No IRD approval is required in advance, but the payer must retain the certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory NRWT 15%; DTA rates typically 10% or 5% (e.g. Australia 5%, US 5%). Interest: statutory NRWT 15%; the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) may substitute for NRWT at 2% if the payer is an IRD-approved issuer; DTA rates typically 10% or 0% (e.g. US 0% for portfolio interest, Australia 10% for interest).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Local File/Master File requirement; Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting applies to NZ resident multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of NZ$130 million or more. Transfer pricing documentation is expected for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding NZ$1 million in aggregate (low-risk threshold) and must be prepared contemporaneously for any material transaction.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are enacted in New Zealand. However, the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG 1, Income Tax Act 2007) and related judicial doctrines require genuine economic substance and commercial purpose. A company without real business activity may be treated as a shell, and arrangements designed to avoid tax can be voided by the Commissioner. Actual die-casting manufacturing and tampo printing in NZ constitute real economic substance; no additional ESR filing is required.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting sales revenue from die-cast scale model sales, falsifying purchase invoices, or deliberately understating taxable income to reduce corporate tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty up to 150% of the tax shortfall, plus use-of-money interest; criminal prosecution may result in fines up to NZ$250,000 for a company (and NZ$50,000 for individuals) and/or imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or knowingly assist in evasion face personal criminal prosecution, civil recovery of unpaid tax and penalties, and disqualification. Inland Revenue can seek orders restraining departure from New Zealand (travel bans) and asset freezing orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement Without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating a New Zealand company solely to benefit from a DTA, access NZ customs/jurisdiction branding, or launder funds while maintaining no real die-casting plant, employees, or managerial presence in New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may apply s BG 1 to disregard the arrangement, deny treaty benefits, assess full New Zealand tax at 28% on all income, and impose a shortfall penalty of 40% to 150% depending on carelessness or fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable as shadow principals for the company's tax liabilities under the Companies Act 1993 (s 376) if they allowed the company to trade with no substance; civil penalties and costs orders may attach.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing cross-border related-party purchases of zinc alloy, tampo printing inks, or commissioned marketing fees at non-arm's length levels, shifting profit outside New Zealand to a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may re-determine the taxable income under the arm's length principle, raising an assessment with shortfall penalties: 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, and 150% for fraud/evasion; plus UOMI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign defective transfer pricing documentation or approve redirected profits face personal liability for the penalty amount if corporate veil-piercing applies; criminal liability may arise for evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing false financial statements to banks or PayPal, hiding the beneficial ownership of the NZ Ltd, or conducting cash/wire transactions that raise money laundering red flags (e.g. inexplicable layering through a shell holding company).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breaches of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 can attract civil penalties up to NZ$2 million per contravention for a body corporate; criminal penalty for a financing of terrorism offence is up to NZ$2 million and 7 years imprisonment. Additionally, directors face disqualification under the Insolvency Act 2006.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for civil penalty orders and may be banned from managing companies. Travel bans can be imposed while criminal investigations are pending; individuals involved in laundering proceeds of crime are liable to imprisonment up to 7 years.
